# javaabu/auth

> Multi-auth for Laravel: any number of user types (public users, admins, …), each with its own guard, password broker, routes, pages and features. Login, registration, password reset, email verification, password confirmation, TOTP two-factor authentication with recovery codes (off, optional or required per type), passkeys (laravel/passkeys), profile and security pages (password, two-factor, passkeys, browser sessions, API tokens), API authentication with Sanctum, Passport or both, account status and lockout, and admin actions on other accounts behind javaabu/permissions permissions. Pages in Blade (javaabu/forms) and Inertia React (@javaabu/forms) that work in Dhivehi and right to left. Not built on laravel/fortify, but uses its 2FA column format and route names.

Paths are relative to this file. In a project, that's vendor/javaabu/auth/.

## Rules

- A user type is configured in `config('javaabu-auth.user_types')` or with `Javaabu\Auth\UserTypes::register()`: `model`, `guard`, `passwords`, `route_name`, `home`, `views`, `layouts`, `username`, `features`, `two_factor`, `max_login_attempts`, `login_methods`. The first type is the default.
- Never assume the `web` guard, `App\Models\User` or `route('login')`. Get the type with `UserTypes::get()`, `for($user)`, `forGuard()` or `fromRequest()`, and URLs with `$type->route('login')`, `$type->homeUrl($user)`.
- Register a type's routes with `Route::authRoutes('admin', ['prefix' => 'admin'])`; nothing loads automatically. Route names get the type's `route_name` prefix: `admin.login`, `admin.password.request`, `admin.profile.edit`.
- Protect app pages with `auth.type:{type}` (guard, account status, verified email, required password change, required 2FA). Ask for the password again with `auth.password.confirm:{type}`, which is kept per type.
- Change behaviour by binding the action contracts (`CreatesNewUsers`, `ResetsUserPasswords`, `UpdatesUserPasswords`, `UpdatesUserProfileInformation`, `DeletesUsers`), extending a controller set in `config('javaabu-auth.controllers')`, or rebinding the responses (`LoginResponse`, …). Don't write auth controllers by hand.
- Alternative login methods implement `Javaabu\Auth\Contracts\LoginMethod` and finish with `Javaabu\Auth\Actions\StartAuthenticatedSession`; never call `Auth::login()` directly.
- User models extend `Javaabu\Auth\Models\User`, or use the traits in `Javaabu\Auth\Concerns` with their contracts. Tables use `Javaabu\Auth\Schema\UserSchema::columns()`.
- Two-factor columns and encryption match laravel/fortify. Passkeys use the package's `passkeys` table with `user_type`; don't publish laravel/passkeys' migration or routes.
- API tokens: the model's `HasApiTokens` (Sanctum or Passport) decides the driver; set `config('javaabu-auth.api')` with `php artisan auth:install --api=…`. Sanctum token logins come from `Route::authApiRoutes()`.
- Account actions (unlock, reset 2FA, require a new password, log out everywhere) come from `Route::userAccountActions()`, behind `auth.*` gate abilities taking `[$type, $account]` and the `{action}_{type plural}` permissions; run `php artisan permissions:sync`.
- Pages render with `config('javaabu-auth.views')` (`blade` or `inertia`, per type with `views`). Blade pages extend `javaabu-auth.layouts.auth` / `.account`. React pages are `auth::Login`, …, `auth::Settings/Security`, resolved with javaabu/manifest's `resolvePage()`. Override with `vendor:publish --tag=auth-views` or `php artisan manifest:override auth <file>`.
- Packages add links to the account navigation with `UserTypes::accountLink('mobile-number', 'Mobile number')` (every type that has the route) or `$type->accountLink(…)`; pages get them as `account_links`. Render package account pages with the type's `account` layout and `PageData::shared()` props.
- Every user-facing string is an English `__()` key with Dhivehi in `lang/dv.json`; app overrides go in the app's `lang/dv.json`. Use logical utilities (`ms-`, `text-start`) only.
